articles.summary: Según el acta de Hernández Maeso, los agentes tuvieron que "sujetar y apartar" al director deportivo del Valencia que gritaba "¡No es falta, no es falta!"
articles.body: El acta arbitral del Valencia-Real Madrid reflejó un incidente protagonizado por el director deportivo valencianista, Braulio Vázquez, durante el descanso del encuentro disputado en Mestalla. El colegiado Francisco José Hernández Maeso recogió en el apartado de observaciones que fue necesaria la intervención de agentes del Cuerpo Nacional de Policía para poner fin a la situación producida en el túnel de vestuarios. Según el relato del árbitro, los hechos ocurrieron al término de la primera parte, cuando Vázquez se encontraba en la zona de acceso a los vestuarios. Hernández señala que el director deportivo valencianista protagonizó un altercado con el árbitro asistente número uno, Iván Massó, llegando a encararse con él mientras repetía en tono exaltado: "¡No es falta, no es falta! ¡Vaya tela!". Se entiende que Braulio se refería en sus protestas a la acción que dio origen al primer gol, una carga de Maffeo sobre Mbappé, que sancionó con falta y tarjeta amarilla. El lanzamiento del libre directo se estrelló en la barrera, pero el rechace cayó en Valverde que anotó el primer tanto de disparo cruzado. El colegiado añade que, cuando pasó junto al dirigente del Valencia, este también se dirigió a él en varias ocasiones empleando las mismas expresiones y manteniendo una actitud exaltada. La redacción del acta va más allá y detalla que la situación obligó a intervenir a efectivos policiales presentes en el estadio. "Fue necesaria la intervención de agentes del Cuerpo Nacional de Policía, quienes procedieron a su identificación y tuvieron que sujetarlo y apartarlo del lugar para poner fin al incidente", escribió Hernández en el documento oficial remitido tras el encuentro Tras el encuentro, el jugador del Valencia Guido Rodríguez, ya había hecho referencia a lo sucedido durante una entrevista con DAZN al preguntarle por lo sucedido. El centrocampista argentino evitó profundizar en el incidente porque cuando llegó más tarde al túnel de vestuarios.

articles.title: 'Curtains for Robinson' or can floundering Aberdeen boss survive?
articles.summary: Will the "unacceptable" 4-0 home defeat to fellow strugglers Hibernian signal the end of Stephen Robinson's Aberdeen tenure?
articles.body:
Stephen Robinson has vowed to "keep fighting until told otherwise" as his Aberdeen future hangs by a thread following the "unacceptable" 4-0 defeat by Hibernian.

The Pittodrie manager, who was already under intense pressure, had labelled the visit of Marink Reedijk's side - bottom of the table going into the game - as a must-win.

But his bedraggled team were no match for Hibs, and home fans began streaming for the exit at 2-0 down. By the bitter end of the four-goal mauling, chants of "You're getting sacked in the morning" rang out and those that had stayed vented their ire at a miserable-looking Robinson as he made a beeline for the tunnel.

"Stephen Robinson looks beleaguered down there, a man lost," said Aberdeen legend Willie Miller on BBC Sportsound.

The television cameras then panned to Adrian Bevington, the chief executive appointed in September. A month and a half into the job, he has a big decision to make.

Aberdeen now occupy the relegation play-off place, above only Kilmarnock, after a fourth Scottish Premiership defeat in five.

"I don't know [what the implications may be], I don't make that decision," Robinson said post-match. "I'm Aberdeen manager until told otherwise, I'll keep fighting until told otherwise.

"The performance isn't acceptable, the result isn't acceptable.

"It's the story of the season - if you don't take chances, you lose matches. They had five opportunities, scored four of them. That's the difference."

Former Celtic striker Chris Sutton says it feels like "the club is too big for him, the job is too big for him" and suggested the 51-year-old should "do the honourable thing and walk away", but is "probably going to end up getting the sack".

Rampant Hibs off bottom as Robinson's Aberdeen gloom deepens

Pre-match, the Aberdeen head coach had insisted his players knew the "magnitude" of the situation in front of them.

It didn't seem that way, as they went on to turn in an insipid performance, spurning a few decent opportunities before completely capitulating in the second half.

"It's utterly embarrassing," said Miller.

"They look ashen-faced down there. Robinson was depressed after the Falkirk result [1-0 home defeat] and this one is 10 times worse than that, so I don't know how he'll cope with it."

Robinson, appointed in March, has won just six of 21 league games, losing 11. He steadied the ship last season and steered the club clear of relegation worries, but the trap door has already started to loom.

"He has now made sweeping changes in personnel," Miller said. Fifteen players were signed in the summer. Few have made a positive impact.

"Recruitment is vital and when you look at the performances, the recruitment is poor. The players aren't up to scratch, not up to playing at this level and dealing with high-ish expectations," added Miller.

"I'm not talking about trophies, I'm talking about being in the top six and they're nowhere near that. There's major issues that have to be confronted."

Should Aberdeen dispense with Robinson, it would be their sixth managerial change since Derek McInnes left in 2021.

"I don't know [if he can survive this]," Miller added. "He had an opportunity to get to a cup final. They lost that and then get beat 4-0 by a team at the bottom of the table. Put all that together and there's major decisions to be made over this weekend."

Robinson 'not the right fit' for Aberdeen

Aberdeen have now lost four consecutive games in all competitions. At home, they've won two of seven in the league.

They've scored three goals in their past six league outings at Pittodrie, and they all came in the 3-1 win over St Mirren. The Dons are the joint lowest scorers in the league, alongside the Buddies, on 12 goals.

"You do get that feeling it could now be curtains for Robinson," former Scotland midfielder Michael Stewart said on Premier Sports.

"You get a sense sometimes with the nature of a result, it can be what finally pushes something to the point of no return."

His colleagues Alan Hutton and Charlie Mulgrew, a former Aberdeen defender, concurred.

"I felt like [the players] gave up towards the end," Hutton added, with Hibs scoring twice in the last six minutes. "The reaction of the fans, to boo the team and manager, doesn't look great coming into an international break.

"I've watched Aberdeen this season and I don't see an identity from them, I don't see a clear plan moving forward. There's been so much change in terms of personnel and formation. I just don't see it in the pitch, it's as if they're hoping for something to happen."

Northern Irishman Robinson earned the move to Pittodrie on the back of three successive top-six finishes and a League Cup triumph with St Mirren, but he wasn't a popular choice among some Aberdeen fans.

"I don't think Robinson seems to be the right fit for Aberdeen," Mulgrew said.

"His style with his St Mirren team, it's not what the fans at Pittodrie like to see on the pitch. They tried to go with wingers today but there was no end product, they huffed and puffed.

"Chances fell to [Kevin] Nisbet but he looked like he had no confidence. I think that'll be the end for Robinson."

Colin: We're a relegation waiting to happen. I wasn't thrilled to see Robinson to take over but I expected him at least to make us hard working and organised. But I can't believe how sloppy and passive we were. And, apart from Ayoub Mouloua, there's no pace, creativity or goal threat from anywhere.

Bill: Robinson was a panic purchase at the time. He has been always well out of his depth and he must go but the problem is higher than him, which needs to be acknowledged by the board.

Mikey: Changing so many players at once was a mistake. Brought too much risk and placed too much trust in a manager just in the door who was stepping up a level. He looks like doesn't want to be there any more.

Greig: Time is up, it's clearly not working. Zero improvement in the playing squad/performances this season. It runs deeper than Robinson, six managers, likely seven since Dave Cormack took over and McInnes left the club. Serious questions have to be asked about the club's direction from the top down.

Sandy: Robinson says he will keep on fighting I see no signs of fighting. I sincerely hope Dave Cormack has someone on the backburner or it's Championship for us next season.

articles.title: Coach of NJ's top girls soccer team suspended for playoff game after champagne bottle celebration
articles.summary: Video shows New Jersey coach Karen Anderson popping a champagne bottle on school property after her 100th career win, triggering a suspension.
articles.body: A New Jersey girls' soccer coach has been suspended for a playoff game for celebrating a milestone victory with a champagne bottle. Paul VI coach Karen Anderson was seen on video celebrating her 100th career win, a 2-0 win over Notre Dame in the South Jersey, Non-Public A quarterfinals, by what appeared to be popping the bottle on school property after the game. So, perhaps the punishment is rather lenient. Anderson told the outlet that she was "not surprised" that the video was coming to light "given our success." articles.title: Lane Kiffin, LSU vs. DeBoer, Alabama Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: No. 9 Alabama has dealt a serious blow to No. 15 LSU's hopes of making the College Football Playoff in Lane Kiffin's first season as head coach.
articles.body:
No. 9 Alabama has dealt a serious blow to No. 15 LSU's hopes of making the College Football Playoff in Lane Kiffin's first season as head coach.

Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell threw three touchdowns as Kalen DeBoer led his team to a 31-13 win Saturday in Death Valley.

Kiffin is now 0-6 in his head coaching career against Alabama.

The Crimson Tide and Tigers were listed at No. 5 and No. 14, respectively, in the first CFP selection committee rankings. LSU is now in danger of missing the playoff altogether after conceding their third loss of the season.

Here's a look at the top offensive performers and highlights from Saturday's matchup in Baton Rouge.

LSU started out strong by forcing the Crimson Tide to go three and out on their second play of the game.

It was Alabama that scored the first touchdown of the day, however, after a successful handoff fake set up Ryan Coleman-Williams to jog into the endzone in his first game back from a knee procedure .

LSU's final two offensive drives of the first half ended with Sam Leavitt throwing an incompletion on 4th and four followed by an interception.

LSU opened the third quarter on a 10-point run capped off by a Dilin Jones rushing touchdown to secure their first lead of the game.

That advantage didn't last for long. It took Alabama just five plays to advance 75 yards on an answering drive that ended with a touchdown pass from Russell.

LSU's hopes of comeback fell apart as both the offense and defense struggled in the fourth quarter.

Russell found Cederian Morgan in the endzone on a 25-yard dime. Alabama's defense then sacked Leavitt to force a turnover on downs and set up another Crimson Tide touchdown drive.

LSU outgained Alabama by 457 yards to 285 yards but went 0-for-4 on fourth down attempts in the loss.

Alabama will look to secure a spot in the playoff by riding the momentum from Saturday's win into another road game next weekend at Vanderbilt.

LSU has no room for error and a challenging schedule coming up. The Tigers, which have yet to secured a ranked win this season, are scheduled for a home game against No. 7 Texas and a road contest at No. 13 Tennessee over the next two weeks.

articles.title: Foggy FA Cup tie: How Altrincham v Notts County was described despite poor visibility
articles.summary: BBC Sport commentator Steve Bower gives an insight into trying to commentate when thick fog engulfs a stadium and you can barely see the action.
articles.body:
One of the most important attributes for a commentator is to be able to see the action you are trying to describe but that became a luxury for BBC Sport's Steve Bower when Altrincham hosted Notts County in an FA Cup tie on Saturday.

As thick fog enveloped the Moss Lane ground, he could barely see what was going on in a first-round game being televised live on BBC Two.

"One of the more challenging of my long career, that's about 35 years now," said Bower about the experience.

"I was reminded by a colleague - maybe I'm a jinx - that we had a similar thing on the BBC about three years ago when we did York against Wigan in the first round and the fog came in.

"Tonight was worse. From where we were, opposite the dugouts, once the play went to the centre circle and beyond, we couldn't see a thing.

"We couldn't see which team had the ball, let alone which player had the ball after about the 60th minute. Bearing in mind it went to extra-time, it was challenging.

"I just kept looking down at my phone and it was text message after text message from people saying, 'You're sounding great, but I can't see a thing'. In the end, you have to roll with it and do the best you can."

Notts County progress in FA Cup tie no-one could see

National League Altrincham were on for an upset when they took a 2-1 lead against the League One side but a late Callum Roberts equaliser for County took the game to extra-time before the visiting side won on penalties.

"The frustrating thing is that for an hour it was a really good FA Cup tie, it had everything," said Bower.

"It was on for another giant-killing script but then the frustrating thing is that it becomes a non-event because, without stating the obvious, people can't see half of it.

"Also, it's not then about the tactics, or the shape of it, or the aggression, or the effort because you just can't see it. As a spectacle in trying to describe a game like you normally would, it's impossible."

Bower's radio colleagues were not faring much better as they tried to work out what was going on.

"I can just about see the bright white numbers on their shirts, but I am struggling to see what is happening on the far side of the pitch," said BBC Radio Nottingham commentator Adam Hassell.

Former Notts County striker Mark Stallard, who was also speaking on BBC Radio Nottingham, said: "We're looking around, and here in the press box no-one knows where the ball is! It's like a spot-the-ball competition.

"I played in the Notts County cup side against Wimbledon when it was abandoned - they equalised in the second half and I didn't see any of it!"

Stallard later said: "We genuinely cannot see the linesman or the players on the far side. It's slightly farcical having to commentate for radio listeners."

The managers of both teams were on the touchline but even they were struggling as tactics went out of the window.

"[Notts County boss] Martin Paterson said credit to Altrincham, they were the better team in the first half and, as for the second, I couldn't see it. He was laughing," said Bower.

"Neil Gibson, the Altrincham manager, was saying, 'We were trying to get down to pitchside to look tactically at what they had done after those four substitutions. Have they changed shape? Is it a back four? Have they gone to a box midfield? But we just couldn't see'.

"So even from a tactical point of view, the players had to stop playing long diagonal passes and things like that because they couldn't see, they were just having to play short five, 10 yard passes so the game changed in that sense as well.

"It was very, very close to getting called off."

Bower said some of the players told him they couldn't see both goals or the corner flags from the centre circle.

"It will live long in the memory, that's for sure," said Bower. "Even on the penalties, you were having to rely on the crowd's reaction before committing to the tale.

"You couldn't see the goalkeeper's save, for instance, until the first replay came in."

The penalties took place in front of Altrincham fans and, while Bower had replays to call on, the Notts County fans "couldn't have seen anything" from the other end as they had to go on "crowd reaction".

"Obviously, the Altrincham fans all had their phones on with the lights trying to put the Notts County players off as well in the fog. A unique evening all around."

articles.title: LaNorris Sellers limps game-winning TD into the end zone as No. 21 South Carolina downs Texas A&M
articles.summary: Sellers left for the locker room right before halftime due to an ankle injury.
articles.body:
The No. 21 South Carolina Gamecocks pulled off the 17-9 comeback win over Texas A&M Saturday night.

South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers went to halftime early due to an ankle injury. He started the second half, but wasn't his usual dual-threat self because the injury was clearly still affecting him.

With just 1:19 left in the game, Sellers took off for a 41-yard rushing touchdown (just his second rush of the second half).

Sellers limped into the end zone and needed help from teammates and staff to get to the bench.

The South Carolina quarterback was injured with just under 5 ½ minutes to go in the first half. Sellers was sacked and took a hit from the front and the back, and it looked like a defender may have rolled up on his left ankle.

Gamecocks head coach Shane Beamer confirmed at halftime that Sellers had an ankle injury, said that the team was worried about it, and that the quarterback was getting X-rays.

After halftime, Beamer said the X-rays were negative and that Sellers would give it a go. The broadcast noted that during warmups, Sellers' throws didn't look good and that the ankle was clearly affecting him.

The dual-threat QB is known for using his legs. He had four rushes in the first half, and only one in the second before his touchdown. Sellers finished with 34 yards and a score on six carries.

After the game, Beamer spoke about how much his team fought and the grit it showed, and he applied those traits to Sellers.

"I mean, what do you say? What a warrior he [Sellers] is. He didn't even know if he was going to be able to play in the second half, and for him to go out there and gut it out like we did and have a touchdown run there at the end of the game… …I'm glad he's on our side, that's all I know."

"I mean, what do you say? What a warrior he [Sellers] is. He didn't even know if he was going to be able to play in the second half, and for him to go out there and gut it out like we did and have a touchdown run there at the end of the game…

…I'm glad he's on our side, that's all I know."

South Carolina began the season 2-3, but has rattled off four consecutive wins, all in conference play. Sellers is a large reason why.

The quarterback threw for 301 yards and 3 touchdowns, with 2 interceptions, and added 96 yards and 2 touchdowns on the ground in South Carolina's win over Oklahoma last week.

Sellers has had at least 96 rushing yards in three of his last five games, showing how important his legs are not only to his game but to the South Carolina offense as a whole.

This season, the South Carolina QB has now thrown for 1,849 yards with 16 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Sellers has run the ball 98 times for 603 yards and 6 scores.

The Gamecocks are now 6-3 and will take on Arkansas on the road next week, with everyone wondering what the QB's status will be after the adrenaline of Saturday's win wears off.

Texas A&M drops to 4-5. The Aggies return home next week to host No. 13 Tennessee.

articles.title: No. 5 Alabama dominates fourth quarter, significantly dents No. 14 LSU's playoff hopes in 31-13 win
articles.summary: The Tigers failed on all four of their fourth-down attempts and scored just one TD on four red zone trips.
articles.body:
LSU's chances of making the College Football Playoff in Lane Kiffin's first season are now incredibly faint.

No. 5 Alabama took over in the fourth quarter in a 31-13 win over the No. 14 Tigers . The Tide scored 21 straight points after LSU took its first lead of the game to turn a close game into a blowout.

The Tide led 17-13 early in the fourth quarter and they seized control after forcing a three-and-out deep in LSU territory. The fourth-and-1 might have been tempting enough for Kiffin to consider going for it, but he decided to punt from his own 16-yard line.

Alabama's Ryan Coleman-Williams, making his return after missing nearly a month with a knee injury, was back to receive the punt. He promptly returned the kick 32 yards to the LSU 25-yard line. The Tigers netted six yards on the kick.

And on the very next play, Keelon Russell found Cederian Morgan for a two-score lead.

Kiffin soon faced another fourth-down decision after Morgan's TD. After a first-down sack put the Tigers behind the chains, LSU had fourth-and-10 at its own 25-yard line with just over eight minutes to go. This time, Kiffin chose to go for it.

Sam Leavitt was sacked for the second time in four plays.

Three plays after that sack, Russell threw his third touchdown of the game when he found Kaleb Edwards on the sideline for a 4-yard score.

After LSU won five straight games over the Crimson Tide from 2003 through 2007, Alabama has now won 16 of the last 20 matchups in the series. And LSU is just 2-7 in Baton Rouge over those 20 games.

LSU's fourth-down and red-zone struggles

You don't have to look too far to see how the game slipped away from LSU.

The Tigers went for it on fourth down four times. They failed to convert all four of those attempts. LSU also entered the red zone four times. The Tigers scored just one touchdown on those four trips.

The first fourth-down failure came in the second quarter after LSU had kicked a short field goal on its first drive and missed a 56-yard attempt on its second before Alabama went up 10-3.

Trailing by seven and needing four yards for a first down at the Alabama 9-yard line, Kiffin kept his offense on the field. However, Leavitt's pass to Trey'Dez Green was broken up and fell incomplete.

LSU had another chance to tie the game before halftime, but Leavitt was intercepted by Luke Metz with 28 seconds to go before the break. And Kiffin wasn't shy about pinning the blame for that pick on his quarterback, either.

Leavitt finished 35-of-47 passing for 380 yards but failed to find the end zone. All but seven of those completions went to three players; Jackson Harris had 11 catches, Green had 10 and RB Dilin Jones had seven.

LSU wasn't simply throwing a lot because the game got away from it in the fourth quarter, either. The Tigers struggled to run the ball, as they finished with 33 carries for 77 yards. Thanks to four sacks, Leavitt rushed 15 times for 16 yards.

Saturday's game was also his seventh of the season with an interception. If he adds to that total in the next two weeks, LSU's chances of making the playoff are likely shot.

The Tigers host No. 7 Texas in Week 11 before visiting No. 13 Tennessee in Week 12. Wins over both of those teams may very well be enough to get LSU into the playoff if the Tigers finish 9-3.

But the margin for error is now gone. Had LSU beaten Alabama, it could afford a loss to either Texas or Tennessee and still feel pretty good about its playoff chances. Instead, the Tigers have to be perfect the rest of the way. And given what we've seen over the first three quarters of the season, it's hard to see how LSU can do that.

articles.title: Ryan Day's Ohio State Contract Buyout Details After Back-to-Back Losses vs. Oregon, USC
articles.summary: No. 12 Ohio State was taken down by No. 23 Oregon on Saturday, losing by the final score of 41-28 at Ohio Stadium.
articles.body:
No. 12 Ohio State was taken down by No. 23 Oregon on Saturday, losing by the final score of 41-28 at Ohio Stadium.

With the Buckeyes suffering their second consecutive defeat after falling to USC on Oct. 31, it isn't hard to imagine the buzz surrounding head coach Ryan Day's job security continuing to grow.

The buyout on Day's contract is worth $75 million, according to Fox Sports .

He previously signed a seven-year deal with the Buckeyes that runs through the 2031 season in Feb. 2025.

This year, Ohio State dropped to 6-3 with Saturday's loss. The Buckeyes also own a 4-2 record in the Big Ten.

Ohio State now holds +7500 odds to win the national championship, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

It's worth noting that Ohio State starting quarterback Julian Sayin has missed the team's past two games due to a right arm injury , but the Buckeyes were facing an Oregon squad that was also without first-string passer Dante Moore on Saturday.

Luke Fahey started at quarterback for Ohio State in place of Sayin, finishing 36-of-50 for 360 yards and two touchdowns compared to one interception.

The Buckeyes took a 14-0 lead at the end of the first quarter, but Oregon scored 38 unanswered points to turn the game into a blowout. The Ducks thrived offensively, racking up 395 total yards without committing a turnover.

Ohio State standout receiver Jeremiah Smith was visibly frustrated in the third quarter of the contest.

The Buckeyes will attempt to get back on track against Northwestern on Nov. 14.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith, Dylan Raiola's Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Oregon-Ohio State
articles.summary: Dylan Raiola and the Oregon Ducks picked up an emphatic road victory over Jeremiah Smith and the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
Dylan Raiola and the Oregon Ducks picked up an emphatic road victory over Jeremiah Smith and the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday afternoon.

Raiola led the Ducks to a 41-point performance to keep their bleak College Football Playoff hopes alive.

Smith had another 100-yard performance, but there were gaps in the game in which he didn't make an impact inside the Buckeyes offense.

Raiola led the Ducks to 38 unanswered points between the second and fourth quarters.

The Ducks were down by 14 points early, but they rallied and had a three-point lead at halftime.

Raiola unleashed a pair of touchdown passes in the third quarter to further open up the advantage in Columbus.

Raiola's fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Brandon Smith sealed the victory.

Smith scored a late touchdown and put up 133 yards on seven receptions, but he wasn't able to help the Buckeyes stay in the game.

Ohio State's offense struggled in long stretches for the second straight week with Luke Fahey at quarterback. That left Smith visibly frustrated in the second half.

The talk surrounding Smith after Saturday's loss was whether or not he should skip the remainder of the regular season to prepare for the 2027 NFL draft.

Smith is still viewed as a potential No. 1 overall pick in April, but with the way Ohio State is playing, he is likely out of the Heisman Trophy discussion.

Oregon is now 6-3 with an outside chance to qualify for the CFB Playoff, but it needs to win out to have a chance. The same is true about the 6-3 Buckeyes, but their outlook is bleaker given what we saw on Saturday.

articles.title: Celta - Levante | Reacción o irse con inquietud al parón: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: Los dos equipos necesitan un triunfo. Días difíciles en el Celta tras caer ante el Rayo y el Union Saint-Gilloise. El Levante, en puestos de descenso, busca su primera victoria a domicilio
articles.summary: Los dos equipos necesitan un triunfo. Días difíciles en el Celta tras caer ante el Rayo y el Union Saint-Gilloise. El Levante, en puestos de descenso, busca su primera victoria a domicilio
articles.body: Con prisas por ganar. Con algo de urgencia por recuperar el pulso de la competición. Con cierta necesidad. Celta y Levante se miden en el estadio de Balaídos con una idea clara: llevarse los tres puntos en juego y olvidar el bache por el que están atravesando en los últimos tiempos. Un triunfo para volver a sonreír, un triunfo para mirar el porvenir con más optimismo, un triunfo para marcharse al parón mucho más tranquilos. Necesitan los gallegos cerrar positivamente una semana en la que salieron goleados de Vallecas y, posteriormente, se complicaron la vida en la Europa League con una nueva derrota, aunque inmerecida, ante el Union Saint-Gilloise. A su vez, deben hacerse fuertes en Balaídos para mantenerse en la zona templada de la tabla. Convocó Claudio Giráldez a todos sus futbolistas disponibles, ante las ausencias de los lesionados Borja Iglesias, Miguel Román, Álvaro Núñez, Starfelt y Jones El-Abdellaoui. Como siempre, algo habitual en el técnico, habrá rotaciones en un once en el que la presencia de Driouech podría ser una de las novedades. Buscará la tercera victoria de la temporada ante el Celta. El equipo granota llega a esta duodécima jornada en posiciones de descenso con diez puntos, empatado con el Elche, que se sitúa fuera de la zona roja. Los de Luís Castro afrontan esta fecha tras caer derrotados ante el Atlético (0-2) la pasada jornada en casa y haber perdido también con anterioridad contra la Real Sociedad en el feudo donostiarra. Aún sin ganar fuera de casa, el Levante intentará alcanzar las primeras tres unidades en Balaídos, donde ya logró la temporada pasada un triunfo vital para conseguir la permanencia en Primera. Con tan solo una ausencia confirmada por molestias musculares, la de Manu Sánchez, los granotas recuperan a Enzo Bardeli, tras regresar a los entrenamientos aunque, según el técnico luso, no está para jugar el partido completo. Jutglà vs Iván Romero. Serán dos de las referencias en ataque. Ambos han participado en los 11 encuentros del campeonato que se han disputado y tienen números anotadores muy parecidos. Dos goles ha celebrado el delantero Celta por uno más que suma el del Levante. La derrota en la Europa League hizo daño y el Celta necesita reaccionar ante su afición. Otro mal resultado complicaría el parón de los gallegos. Enfrente, el Levante, un equipo en descenso que será un rival duro de pelar. También tienen necesidades los granotas a los que, además, les está costando fuera de casa, donde sólo han sumado tres puntos en lo que va de campeonato.

articles.title: CFB Playoff Picture, Standings and Bracket Predictions After Week 10 of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The Utah Utes and Alabama Crimson Tide reaffirmed their positions inside the top five in the College Football Playoff rankings on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
The Utah Utes and Alabama Crimson Tide reaffirmed their positions inside the top five in the College Football Playoff rankings on Saturday afternoon.

Utah pulled out a rivalry win at home over the BYU Cougars to remain undefeated, and at minimum, remain inside the top three in the rankings.

Alabama went on the road and picked up a huge road win over the LSU Tigers to justify their No. 5 spot in the CFB Playoff rankings.

On the other end of the rankings, the Ohio State Buckeyes' loss to the Oregon Ducks will take them out of contention after starting the weekend at No. 12.

No. 3 Utah Remains Undefeated With Win Over No. 9 BYU

Utah overcame the last massive hurdle on its schedule with a rivalry win over BYU on Saturday afternoon.

The Utes took over in the second half with a pair of touchdowns and three interceptions off BYU's Bear Bachmeier.

Utah now sits at 9-0 with a clear path to a first-round bye in the CFB Playoff.

A potentially tricky road trip to Arizona awaits next week, but the Wildcats have already lost to BYU and Texas Tech in Big 12 play.

Utah is two games up on everyone other than Texas Tech in the Big 12 standings, so it is almost assured of a spot in the Big 12 Championship Game.

A Big 12 Championship Game win would allow the Utes to have an even stronger resume to compare against whichever teams end up fighting for the top four seeds in December.

As for BYU, its playoff chances are in peril. It win drop a few spots from No. 9 in Tuesday's rankings and it doesn't have any big games left.

The best-case scenario for the Cougars would be to win out and find its way into the Big 12 Championship Game for another shot at Utah.

No. 5 Alabama Routs No. 13 LSU In Baton Rouge

Alabama justified its No. 5 spot in the CFB Playoff rankings with a commanding 31-13 win in Baton Rouge.

There were concerns about Alabama's spot in Tuesday's rankings because of their two losses.

However, that seems to have gone out the window, at least for now, with the road win at LSU.

Alabama doesn't have the best resume among the CFB Playoff contenders because it lost to the Georgia Bulldogs and Tennessee Volunteers, but now it has a pair of top-20 wins.

Alabama's goal for the rest of November is to not lose and try to earn a spot in the SEC Championship Game.

A 10-3 Alabama could get into the 12-team playoff field if the third loss occurs in the SEC Championship Game.

LSU's playoff hopes were already on thin ice going into Week 10. The home loss to Alabama likely ends its postseason quest.

No. 12 Ohio State Loses At Home to No. 23 Oregon

Ohio State's playoff hopes were washed away at home on Saturday by the Oregon Ducks.

The Buckeyes gave up 38 unanswered points to Dylan Raiola and Co. in their third loss of the season.

Ohio State has now suffered back-to-back losses and it looks it may struggle just to win multiple additional games.

On the other hand, the Ducks are still barely alive at 6-3 because they will receive a boost in the rankings on Tuesday.

Neither team will be close to the top 12 on Tuesday, but at least for Oregon, there is hope.

articles.title: Vikings Receive Trade Speculation Amid Failed Offensive Experiment
articles.summary: Frustrated by a stagnant offense, Minnesota may shop high-profile signing Jauan Jennings before the deadline to salvage a season defined by elite defense and...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) are the most confounding team in the National Football League through eight weeks of football. They're having as rough a start to a season as you could have with an 86% winning percentage through seven games.

The Vikings fanbase might be the most discontented 6-1 fanbase of a football team in the last decade. The lack of trust in their team revolves around an inept offense squandering one of the best defenses of the last decade.

It's no secret the Vikings should be 7-0 right now and towering over the rest of the NFL. That is, if the team had a fraction of the offense it was expected to have after key offseason additions. One such addition was Minnesota wide receiver Jauan Jennings.

Athlon Sports' Neal Coolong discussed the possibility that the Vikings might consider trading its premiere free agent wide receiver pickup in Jauan Jennings. Here's what Coolong had to say about the potential of a trade.

"The fit in Minnesota hasn't worked the way either side hoped when he signed a one-year deal in May. Jennings has six catches for 54 yards in six games, according to ESPN's team stats, two years after he put up 975 receiving yards in San Francisco.

Side by side with Jordan Addison, the gap in his role is plain. Addison has drawn 32 targets in six games as the No. 2 receiver behind Justin Jefferson. Jennings has 10 over the same number of games, and the Vikings added Odell Beckham Jr. in October, which only crowded the room further.

Jennings' own wishes are the wild card. He effectively vetoed the San Francisco deal, and we wrote that 49ers fans shouldn't hold their breath for a reunion. Minnesota could still find a team he'd accept, especially one with a bigger role to offer."

Jennings is set to miss the Vikings' upcoming Monday Night Football game against the Buffalo Bills with injury. He hasn't done much when healthy either.

What the Vikings could get in return for a trade of Jennings is uncertain, but what is certain is that they're really not getting anything from him when he is on the field. It has been one of, if not the most disappointing developments of the Vikings' 2026 season.

The Vikings have plenty to sort out before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but wide receiver definitely makes the list. We'll see what moves they opt to make or not to make as the trading window comes to a close.

articles.title: McCown, Jenkins account for 6 TDs and Lamar seizes Southland lead with win over Stephen F. Austin

Lamar (8-2, 6-1) entered ranked 13th in the Stats Perform FCS Poll and now sits atop the Southland Conference standings.

Stephen F. Austin (9-1, 6-1) entered ranked second in the Stats Perform poll.

The Cardinals built a 17-0 lead and led by 10 at halftime.

Andres Sandoval kicked a 27-yard field goal near the midway point of the first quarter. McCown led a nine-play, 65-yard drive that ended with his 7-yard scoring pass to Davin Driskell with 2:03 left in the first.

Midway threw the second, Jenkins ran it in from the 3 to end a nine-play, 60-yard drive for the 17-point advantage.

Gavin Rutherford threw a 22-yard scoring pass to Clayton Wayland with 25 seconds before halftime for the Lumberjacks' first score.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 10
articles.summary: SOUTH BEND, Ind. — Thanks to a slate packed with Top 25 showdowns and rivalries, Week 10 commanded a lofty billing as a pivotal Saturday.
articles.body:
SOUTH BEND, Ind. — Thanks to a slate packed with Top 25 showdowns and rivalries, Week 10 commanded a lofty billing as a pivotal Saturday.

Utah kicked off the action with a massive win against BYU, and Arch Manning-led Texas snatched a key result at Missouri. During the afternoon window, however, Ohio State took a crushing loss at the hands of Oregon.

The action rolls along in the evening with top-ranked Miami playing at Notre Dame and a couple of impactful SEC tilts.

This piece will be updated throughout Saturday's action.

As expected, the Holy War—with BYU and Utah both ranked as top-10 teams for the first time in series history—provided some fireworks.

Utah roared out to a 14-0 edge but watched BYU score 20 straight points. Utah regained the lead and added a touchdown to move ahead 28-20, setting up a dramatic final quarter in which Utah's defense took the spotlight.

Bear Bachmeier engineered a 13-play, seven-minute drive inside Utah's five. But then, Trey Reynolds snagged an interception at the goal line to end the threat.

After the Utes couldn't quite run out the clock, a short punt gifted BYU a final opportunity. For a moment, it looked like the Cougars might actually pull off a stunner. In the waning seconds of regulation, Bachmeier rolled right and heaved a pass toward Kyler Kasper in the end zone. Utah's Nate Ritchie jumped in front at the last second for a game-sealing pick.

Utah was far from perfect defensively, but the unit made key plays at key moments. That's the mark of an excellent team.

The problem for Minnesota? Those few connections turned into a career-high 303 yards and three touchdowns for Ty Dieffenbach, who guided the Bruins to a 34-20 road win against the Golden Gophers.

Early on, Dieffenbach found Semaj Morgan for a 54-yard completion that set up UCLA's first touchdown. Late in the game, Dieffenbach hit a streaking Aidan Mizell for a pair of 75-yard scores.

Minnesota fought valiantly, tying the game in the fourth quarter and later trimming UCLA's lead to 24-20.

But those meltdowns on the back end cost Minnesota a shot at the upset.

Amid a season with such incredible highs and crushing lows, this one must've felt cathartic for Arch Manning.

Texas picked up a vital 34-20 win at 18th-ranked Missouri, notching a fourth victory over a Top 25 opponent this season. Manning completed 28-of-38 passes for 297 yards with three touchdowns and zero turnovers.

For a week, at least, the critics—of which I have been—will be quieter.

Yes, a favorable decision on a fumble-or-interception review certainly helped. Also, the road doesn't get easier with a trip to LSU looming. The tone around him and the Horns is liable to change by the week.

Manning, though, put together a strong afternoon to keep Texas solidly in the race for a College Football Playoff bid.

Five weeks ago, I thought the bells were sounding on Shane Beamer's tenure. Already on a burning hot seat, he'd just endured a crushing loss at the hands of Kentucky—after setbacks to Mississippi State and Alabama. Beamer and star defender Dylan Stewart had an argument on the sideline.

Fast-forward to today, and everything is right. South Carolina has ripped off four straight wins, including Saturday's 17-9 triumph over Texas A&M.

LaNorris Sellers punctuated the victory with a 41-yard scamper, hobbling the final few yards for a touchdown as the crowd erupted into a frenzy. He gritted through an ankle injury as the Gamecocks climbed to a now-shocking 6-3 record.

South Carolina, rather suddenly, isn't terribly far from affecting the CFP race.

Georgia still awaits in a couple of weeks, but the 21st-ranked Gamecocks must be taken seriously. What a difference a month has made.

Falling to Oregon isn't absolutely, unequivocally the final nail in the coffin for Ohio State. This season has been filled with chaos, and the Buckeyes still have quality wins against Iowa and Indiana on their résumé.

Fans began streaming out of the Horseshoe as OSU fell behind 38-14 early in the fourth quarter. The offense, understandably, struggled again without quarterback Julian Sayin, flailing in the middle stanzas of the 41-28 loss—one certain to crank up the noise surrounding Ryan Day's job security.

"To lose three games is unacceptable, and I own that," a disappointed Day told reporters after the setback.

The only way Ohio State sneaks back into the CFP conversation is winning out—plausible with Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan to finish— plus help.

And that's not a guarantee to be enough.

Alabama took a 10-3 advantage into the locker room, but LSU flipped the script in the third quarter with a field goal, defensive stop and touchdown.

You would be forgiven if you thought Bama, then trailing 13-10, was in deep trouble. Instead, though, the Crimson Tide dominated the last 17 minutes of the second half on their way to a pivotal 31-13 road win.

On the first snap after LSU jumped ahead, Keelon Russell's 57-yard completion to Rico Scott sparked the Tide. Russell soon connected with Josh Ford for a go-ahead score. Ryan Coleman-Williams' long punt return and Bama forcing a turnover on downs set up two more touchdown passes from Russell.

In a flash, a competitive clash morphed into a blowout.

Not only did the No. 5 Tide put a major dent in LSU's postseason upside, they further padded a résumé the CFP selection committee clearly values.

articles.title: Everything Texas A&M HC, players said after loss to South Carolina
articles.summary: See what Mike Elko and Texas A&M players said after the Aggies' 17-9 loss to South Carolina, including reactions to missed opportunities.
articles.body:
Texas A&M's 17-9 loss to No. 21 South Carolina on Saturday wasn't because the Aggies couldn't move the football. Instead, the biggest questions following the game centered on why that production failed to translate into points.

Texas A&M finished with 457 total yards, controlled possession for nearly 10 additional minutes and received a season-high 137 rushing yards from Rueben Owens II. However, the Aggies couldn't capitalize on several promising drives, repeatedly coming away empty-handed or settling for field goals.

Two false-start penalties near the goal line and a dropped touchdown pass proved particularly costly in the third quarter. Kicker David Olano also missed a 30-yard field goal, his first unsuccessful attempt of the season.

The Aggies carried a 9-7 advantage into the fourth quarter before South Carolina scored 10 unanswered points to secure its fourth consecutive victory. The Gamecocks took the lead on a field goal before quarterback LaNorris Sellers delivered the decisive blow with a 41-yard touchdown run.

For head coach Mike Elko, the result added another difficult chapter to a season that began with College Football Playoff expectations. Texas A&M is now 4-5 overall and guaranteed its first losing SEC record under Elko.

With Tennessee, Oklahoma and Texas remaining on the schedule, the Aggies must win at least two of their final three games to become bowl eligible. Saturday's missed opportunities will undoubtedly remain a major talking point as Texas A&M prepares for its final home stretch.

Here's what Elko and Texas A&M players had to say following Saturday's loss.

Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko initial thoughts after the game

"Another disappointing finish. For a large part of that game, I thought we played the way we wanted to." "Really bad in the red zone. Really bad composure in the second half in the red zone. We can't get down there as much as we did and not come away with points."

"Another disappointing finish. For a large part of that game, I thought we played the way we wanted to."

"Really bad in the red zone. Really bad composure in the second half in the red zone. We can't get down there as much as we did and not come away with points."

"We challenged them to be physical. We thought that would be a big part of the game… We did what we wanted to do until the red area, and in the red area, we couldn't finish."

Mike Elko on the fake field goal attempt

"I thought we had the look. The film will show we had exactly what we wanted. I thought we blocked it how we wanted. Unfortunately, we didn't get the run we needed."

Mike Elko on KJ Edwards & Jamarion Morrow

"KJ (Edwards) had the flu this week. He was on the injury list because of that. Jamarion Morrow is banged up a little bit. He wasn't 100 percent ready to go. We have a ton of confidence in Rueben (Owens)… He was hot out there and ran the ball well."

Mike Elko on Marcel Reed's final two passes

"I thought the first throw to Aaron Gregory, he gave him a chance. It was out of Aaron's reach, but he gave him a chance. That's what you have to do. The second one, it got away from him."

"He was limited. He got rolled up early. He gutted it out, and at halftime, it tightened up on him."

"I thought he played well… I thought that was his best game of the year, and I thought we operated, for the most part, better than we have for most of the year."

Texas A&M linebacker Ray Coney on the mood of the locker room

"It sucks. In the week, you put in so much work, and for three quarters, you see the work paying off. In that fourth, we have continued to get better."

"We have been making progress, but at the same time, a loss is a loss. We have to figure out somehow to claw, dig and find a way to win."

Texas A&M running back Rueben Owens II on his big day

"I had a good two weeks of practice. Coach and my OL gave me the opportunity, and I put it out there."

"We have to win the fourth quarter. That's the bottom line. We have to put it all together."

Contact/Follow us @AggiesWire on X and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Texas A&M news, notes and opinions. Follow Jarrett Johnson on X: @whosnextsports1 .

articles.title: How property, football and politics link Manchester and Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: A closer look at the relationship between Man City's owners and the Manchester political scene.
articles.body:
When Manchester City was found guilty in September of breaching Premier League financial rules, the damning and unprecedented verdict left the football world reeling.

An independent commission said the club had "systematically" broken rules between 2009 and 2018 by inflating sponsorship revenue to disguise secret funding of more than £830m into its football operations.

Speculation is now rife about the level of punishment City will face, although the club denies any wrongdoing and has appealed against the ruling.

While we await the outcome, the historical relationship between City's Abu Dhabi-based owners and Manchester's political elite - including the now Prime Minister Andy Burnham - has been in the spotlight.

There has been a focus on land deals, multimillion-pound regeneration schemes, and more recently, investigations into loans handed out to property companies owned ultimately by City's owner, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

Beyond the on-field success at the Eithad Stadium, what exactly is the Abu Dhabi story in Manchester?

The story began in 2008 when Manchester City was bought by ADUG in a £200m deal. The Citizens were now owned by Sheikh Mansour, the United Arab Emirates deputy prime minister and a member of its ruling family.

Overnight, City had become one of the richest clubs in the world.

In the years that followed, City's new owners spent billions of pounds turning the club into one of European football's powerhouses.

But away from the pitch, the Abu Dhabi investors were showing a wider interest in their new adopted city of Manchester.

In 2014, six years after taking over Manchester City, ADUG entered into a partnership with Labour-led Manchester City Council.

The club and the council already had a close relationship, with Manchester City having signed a 250-year lease for the former City of Manchester Stadium that had been built for the 2002 Commonwealth Games.

The new joint venture was called Manchester Life and, over a decade, it had a plan to build more than 6,000 new homes through investment of up to £1bn.

To date, about 1,500 homes across nine sites have been delivered, with more currently under construction.

ADUG has also financially supported local community facilities, including the East Manchester Leisure Centre, which opened in 2014.

The area around the stadium was also extensively redeveloped into what is now known as the Etihad Campus, which is also home to the Sky Blues' women's and youth teams.

Most recently, Co-op Live - the largest indoor arena in the UK - opened next to Etihad Stadium and became another high-profile development in east Manchester in which ADUG held a significant stake.

Bev Craig, the recently elected Mayor of Greater Manchester, said ADUG had shown a "unique passion" and commitment to Manchester.

Speaking to the BBC in 2024 while in her previous job as leader of Manchester City Council, Craig described City's owners as having been the "catalyst" for "remarkable" regeneration.

However, there have been repeated claims that the city council sold public land to ADUG too cheaply.

In 2022, a report by the University of Sheffield raised questions about the wider public value of the schemes and a lack of transparency surrounding their finances.

These claims are strongly rejected by Manchester's political leaders, including Sir Richard Leese, who led the city council when the ADUG deal was struck in 2014.

"The point is, the investment from Abu Dhabi is what created the value," Sir Richard told the BBC recently.

He stressed, like Craig and the city council itself, that there was no other significant interest in developing the land during a time of recession following the 2008 financial crash.

"It was a time when development in Manchester had stopped," said Sir Richard.

"That deal allowed development to be kick-started - particularly in the Ancoats area."

Certainly the areas around Ancoats and New Islington, which had suffered from the industrial decline of the latter part of the 20th Century, have been transformed.

Critics, though, are quick to point out the lack of any affordable housing within the Abu Dhabi-owned flats and apartments.

The city council, however, says the regeneration has led to more recent developments in the area, and that these do include social and affordable homes.

The agreement made between Manchester City Council and ADUG is known as an "overage" deal.

It means the seller of the land - in this case the local authority - receives extra financial payments in the future if the land increases in value after it is sold.

These payments are a share of the so-called "super profits".

While these sorts of deals can be complex, they have become increasingly common between local authorities and developers.

Manchester City Council said allegations that its deal with ADUG had either not been good for the local authority or its taxpayers had been "debunked repeatedly".

It said the council had made just under £3m in "super-profits" from Abu Dhabi-owned developments so far, and expected another payment soon.

Prof Adam Leaver, co-author of the University of Sheffield report, has argued that commercial secrecy around the arrangements mean it is hard to know if the council has got the best possible deal.

He said it was "not possible" to know how much profit ADUG had made from the developments, compared to that of the city council.

Leaver also challenged the assertion that there had been little other interest in redeveloping Manchester around the time the Manchester Life partnership was formed.

He pointed out that a number of large projects had already been in the pipeline.

Scrutiny of the land development deal and the wider relationship between Manchester City's owners and the city council intensified after Burnham's comments about the club's breaches of Premier League financial rules .

The prime minister and former Greater Manchester mayor said he would be "really concerned" if the club's owners sold up and praised them for being a "huge partner in the building of modern Manchester".

There was an immediate backlash, with some suggesting Burnham was siding with the club.

Downing Street then stated Manchester City was not "above the rules", and stressed the PM had made it clear that the outcome of the "ongoing independent process" must be respected.

Nevertheless, questions remained. It then emerged that Burnham, while in his role as the city region's mayor, had two hospitality dinners with Manchester City's chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak at matches in 2017 and 2018. He also met Al Mubarek at a Global Investment Summit in 2021.

Burnham's political opponents have demanded full transparency over his dealings with Manchester City's owners.

He recently told MPs he was happy for "everything to be set out in full".

There will also be a Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) scrutiny committee investigation into GMCA loans made to property companies - including three controlled by Manchester City's owner - while Burnham was mayor.

More than £1bn was lent to about 50 developers by the Greater Manchester Housing Investment Loan Fund.

Burnham chaired two meetings which approved about £55m in loans to property firms ultimately owned by Man City's owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan.

The decisions were made in public by all members of the GMCA, not the mayor alone.

There is no suggestion of any wrongdoing, but critics have questioned why seemingly wealthy and successful companies needed to borrow public money through the scheme.

Craig said the intense coverage of Manchester's relationship with Abu Dhabi had made "cheap shots" at Burnham and been used to "bash" the city.

She said that were Manchester City to lose its appeal, then it "should face sanctions".

But she was keen to stress that "what was a football story should have stayed a football story".

Not everyone agrees, however, and while the football world holds its breath to find out City's fate, we can also expect the spotlight to remain on the wider relationship between the city of Manchester and the club's owners.

articles.title: Emboldened No. 23 Oregon dominates No. 12 Ohio State, which could already be out of College Football Playoff race
articles.summary: After going down 14-0 in the first quarter, the Ducks scored 38 straight points.
articles.body:
With a bit more than three minutes remaining in the first half Saturday at the Horseshoe, No. 12 Ohio State was up 14-3, and its freshman quarterback, Luke Fahey , was effectively spreading the ball around in his second career start.

But just as No. 23 Oregon hadn't thrown in the towel on what was once billed as a national championship campaign, the three-loss Ducks didn't back down in Columbus.

On fourth-and-9 from their own 31-yard line, they ran a fake punt that resulted in a 30-yard gain, reviving what turned into a 70-yard touchdown drive. A toe-tapping interception soon after set the stage for another Oregon TD, that one the product of a goal-line chess match. The Ducks won that mid-game duel of the minds, thanks to a funky-looking tush push that quieted the Buckeyes faithful.

Dan Lanning's Oregon (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) turned the game upside down with the kind of nothing-to-lose aggression that punched Ryan Day's Ohio State in the mouth.

The Buckeyes (6-3, 4-2) never recovered, suffering a sobering 41-28 defeat that seriously jeopardizes their College Football Playoff chances.

It also guarantees their first three-plus-loss season since 2011, when they went 6-7 under then-interim head coach Luke Fickell in the wake of the "Tattoogate" scandal that led to Jim Tressel's resignation.

Ohio State, which tumbled from the No. 2 spot in the AP Top 25 after falling to a then-unranked USC team on the road last week , has lost back-to-back games. That also hadn't happened in a Buckeyes regular season since that tumultuous 2011 campaign.

Dating back to the end of the 2025 season, the Buckeyes are a jaw-dropping 4-5 in their last nine games against power conference opponents. And, on Saturday, their 12-game home win streak — previously the longest active streak in the Big Ten — came to an end.

Ohio State has cratered in the absence of 2025 Heisman Trophy finalist Julian Sayin, who suffered a serious injury to his throwing arm in a top-five showdown at Indiana on Oct. 17 .

Fahey, Sayin's backup throughout the fall, got the QB1 nod over sophomore Tavien St. Clair, a former five-star recruit who was the Rivals industry ranking's No. 3 QB prospect in the 2025 class . Fahey played valiantly in a 30-18 setback at USC.

The Buckeyes decided to stick with him this week against Oregon , needing the rest of their team to step up around the first-year signal-caller. Initially, that vision came to fruition versus the Ducks.

Ohio State scored touchdowns on two of its first three series. Running back Bo Jackson skirted around the edge and found pay dirt from 16 yards out. His second touchdown was made possible by 32-yard and 41-yard completions: the first on a deep strike to Jeremiah Smith and the next on a short pass fellow wideout Devin McCuin turned into a big gainer.

Lanning decided to take the points early in the second quarter after his offense finally found somewhat of a groove. Facing a fourth-and-2 from the Ohio State 15-yard line, he sent out kicker Gage Hurych for a 33-yard field goal.

Later on in the quarter, after Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola was nearly picked off by Ohio State safety Jaylen McClain, Lanning made the first of his bold decisions.

Rather than punting the ball back to the Buckeyes, and risking the home team adding to its 11-point advantage before intermission, Lanning opted for a fake.

The ball was snapped to Teitum Tuioti. He ran forward prior to lobbing a jump pass to fellow outside linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei. The 6-foot-5, 265-pound Uiagalelei rumbled down the sideline, putting a bow on the chains-moving, 30-yard pickup with a hurdle.

That drive culminated in the first of running back Dierre Hill Jr.'s two rushing scores. Plus, it was the beginning of the Ducks scoring 38 straight points. Ohio State, according to the CBS Sports broadcast, hadn't given up that many unanswered since a 1999 loss at Wisconsin.

Next, first-year Oregon defensive back Devin Jackson made a highlight-reel interception near the sideline, snagging an errant Fahey pass and getting his right cleat down before his left one landed out of bounds.

Quickly, Raiola guided the Ducks downfield, minding the ticking clock in the process. Instead of potentially settling for a field goal on the final play of the first half, Lanning rolled the dice again.

Oregon lined up with only three offensive linemen, spreading out the Buckeyes to the left and right. Tight end Jamari Johnson scurried to take over under center, received the snap and plowed forward, with Raiola helping push him in from behind.

That end-of-half sequence dug the Ducks out of a multi-score hole and vaulted them into a three-point lead, 17-14.

What's more, they got the ball to start the third quarter. They made the most of that opportunity, too. Hill evaded a slew of defenders on a 48-yard touchdown scamper that raised major questions about the Buckeyes' tackling.

That play was a backbreaker for Ohio State. The Buckeyes didn't accomplish much on offense the rest of the way — that was, until garbage time when Fahey fired a pair of touchdown passes.

One of those went to Smith, and the second was hauled in by tight end Nate Roberts. But those points were simply cosmetic. They made things look slightly closer than they actually were.

When it mattered most, Fahey looked like the freshman he is. The Buckeyes turned the ball over on downs four consecutive second-half drives, the first of which saw the former three-star recruit throw behind McCuin on a fourth-and-2.

Meanwhile, Raiola, still starting in place of the injured Dante Moore , finished 25 of 40 with 257 yards and two touchdowns through the air. A one-handed scoring grab from wideout Dakorien Moore wowed. And a screen pass sprung running back Brandon Smith for the Ducks' final TD.

Oregon and Ohio State are trending in opposite directions. Both were preseason national title contenders. Both have lost their starting quarterbacks to severe injuries.

The Ducks' demeanor of late, however, has belied their midseason misfortune.

images.caption: Oregon's Dan Lanning pulled off one of his most impressive coaching jobs to date at Ohio Stadium on Nov. 7, leading the Ducks to a 41-28 win over Ohio State. (AP Photo/Jay LaPrete)

articles.title: Nashville SC eye MLS Cup after record-setting regular season
articles.summary: By Ben WrightCINCINNATI – Nashville SC's historic season keeps rolling.The Boys in Gold capped their record-setting regular-season campaign with a 2-0 Decisi...
articles.body:
CINCINNATI – Nashville SC 's historic season keeps rolling.

The Boys in Gold capped their record-setting regular-season campaign with a 2-0 Decision Day victory over FC Cincinnati , riding a Sam Surridge brace to their 23rd win and an MLS single-season record 77 points.

After winning the 2025 US Open Cup and 2026 Supporters' Shield, Nashville have established themselves amongst the most dominant regular-season teams in league history.

Now, they'll enter the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs as favorites to add another trophy to their collection.

"We come into every season, and we don't put expectations on ourselves, because sometimes those can actually be limiting factors," said head coach B.J. Callaghan.

"What we talk about is making sure that we stick to the way that we prepare, how every single guy prepares himself, and we want to put in the work each and every day. We believe in the work that we're doing; we believe in the group, the collectiveness."

It's fitting that the team whose points record Nashville surpassed was Inter Miami CF .

Since the two clubs entered MLS as expansion teams in 2020, the rivals have been pitted against each other repeatedly. Miami eliminated Nashville from last year's MLS Cup Playoffs en route to winning it all, but Nashville returned the favor in the 2026 Concacaf Champions Cup . Now, they've surpassed Miami's single-season points record (74), set in 2024.

Since Callaghan took over in 2024, Nashville have consistently reached new heights. According to defender Jack Maher , the first SuperDraft pick in club history, that's no coincidence.

"B.J. has transformed our team, and the growth that we've had from 2024 to now is unlike anything I've ever seen before," said the center back.

"This guy eats, sleeps, and breathes soccer, Nashville SC soccer, and that work ethic is now instilled in all of us players... That comes from the top down, and it goes to show how good a coach B.J. is. He's pushed us and pushed us to be better, because he believed in us, and now after 34 games we're really believing in ourselves. That's a recipe made for success."

Nashville SC have built their identity around defensive excellence since entering MLS, dating back to the days of Gary Smith, Joe Willis and Walker Zimmerman .

Even as their attack has reached new heights with a club-record 85 goals across all competitions, the Boys in Gold have remained one of the league's stingiest defensive teams.

Brian Schwake 's 16th clean sheet of the season in Cincinnati tied Tony Meola's MLS record from 2000. Nashville's 17 clean sheets also matched the league record, while their 25 goals conceded were the fewest in a 34-game season.

"For Brian to even be mentioned in that [company] is a tremendous individual accomplishment for him," said Callaghan, a collegiate goalkeeper himself. "You see the way that the back line and him play together... They give him confidence that he can play to them and be himself, because he's got guys in front of him who are willing to do whatever it takes to keep a clean sheet."

Even without injured Defender of the Year candidate Jeisson Palacios , Nashville shut out MVP candidate Evander and Cincinnati's potent attack.

"We have a deep team, especially a deep back line. We have some of the best center backs in the league, hands down," said Maher, who made his 11th regular-season appearance of the year.

"They're playing at levels that I saw prime Walker Zimmerman playing at, and that speaks to how incredible these players and people are. It's a joy to play with them each time I get the opportunity."

With their record-setting season complete, Nashville SC are turning their attention to the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs.

"It's a new season, right?" said Callaghan. "The regular season's over. We'll enjoy it tonight. We're allowed to go up one notch above emotionally neutral, and then we'll get right back to work... We'll be ready to get to work on Monday, with a full focus on making sure that the team is ready to play when the playoffs start."

Club captain Hany Mukhtar , the 2022 Landon Donovan MLS MVP, has led the charge with a team-high 25 goal contributions this season (17g/8a). Maher believes he's deserving of a second MVP award.

"It's been incredible watching him grow over the course of seven years, and I'm biased, but I think he 100% deserves to win the MVP trophy this year," he said.

"When you look over the course of 34 games, what Hany has done as a leader, as a supplier, as a guy who has always come to work in each and every game, he's the best player on the best team in MLS history. I just hope that's something people take into consideration when they're placing their votes."

But Mukhtar has his sights set on an even bigger prize.

"He says, 'Enjoy the three days off, but everyone needs to come back ready and hungry,'" Maher said. "He goes, 'December 18th, that's when everyone can celebrate. Not a day before.'"

articles.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
articles.summary: Seven straight seasons without a playoff berth have left one of MLS' original powerhouses in disrepair, with ownership facing mounting questions about the cl...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production.

While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning.

At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day.

For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses.

Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer.

United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal.

While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport.

The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy.

Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field.

United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14.

Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches.

United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season.

D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team.

United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)

Player development has suffered: United has no representation on the current U.S. under-23, under-20 or under-17 national teams.

Its training complex, in the distant Virginia suburbs, is among the smallest in MLS, and much of the spartan structure is rented to the Washington Spirit, a National Women's Soccer League team.

And in an act of brazen hubris, United is seeking $300 million in public funds to expand capacity and build a roof over the stadium, which opened, in part with public money, just eight years ago. The aim is to attract more events to the venue and has seemingly little to do with MLS ambitions.

The term "Decision Day" (or, in D.C.'s case, "Days") does apply to the organization: It has decisions to make about an uninspiring roster and journeyman coach Rene Weiler, a high-priced hire who has an 8-18-16 record since arriving in July 2025.

In Weiler's defense, injuries ravaged his roster this year. His only two Designated Players, forwards Tai Baribo and Louis Munteanu, missed nine and 13 matches, respectively. (They combined for 22 of the team's 39 goals.)

On Saturday, aside from that duo, goalkeeper Sean Johnson, center back Lucas Bartlett and several others were absent. United had six players on the bench, three short of the maximum.

"It's not that I don't believe in the quality of my squad, but it has to be deeper — more players on a very good level because it's tough to compete weekly with the other opponents, and that is something that we have to try to make better for the future," Weiler said.

Fans have decisions to make, as well, such as deciding whether to continue supporting a club that has fallen into disrepair under an ownership group that doesn't spend enough on many facets of the business and misspends on others.

It had a good thing going in 2018, when Audi Field replaced crumbling RFK Stadium and Wayne Rooney graced the pitch in the first of his two seasons. That now seems like decades ago.

Since 2020, United's place in the Supporters' Shield race, a fancy name for the overall standings, has been:

24th, 16th, 28th, 23rd, 21st, 30th and 28th.

In position to break its playoff drought this fall, United ended the season with six consecutive losses and a 1-8-1 free fall.

The club had only a few true sellouts in 16 matches at Audi Field, which, with about 19,200 seats, is one of MLS' smallest. (D.C. also claimed more than 72,000 for its home date against Inter Miami in Baltimore last spring, though most attendees were there to admire Lionel Messi.)

The NWSL-contending Spirit announced six sellouts in its 15 regular-season games at Audi Field.

On Saturday, United announced a sellout, though thousands of seats were unoccupied on the brisk autumn day.

Levien and his partners bought United in the summer of 2012; the team finished the regular season third in the Supporters' Shield race before being eliminated in the Eastern Conference finals by the Houston Dynamo. It was, indeed, a promising start to the group's reign.

The following year United was the worst in MLS — the first of three bottom-dwelling performances over 13 seasons.

Hope was renewed when Audi Field opened, providing a revenue source that didn't exist at ancient RFK. The Rooney signing and the assembly of an exciting roster brought buzz and success.

But even Rooney failed to lift United beyond the first round of the playoffs, and after less than two years, he returned home. He resurfaced as head coach in Washington in 2022, but it felt more like United's owners wanting to make a splash than hiring a top coach. His tenure ended in 15 months.

This season showed relative promise — getting one of the conference's nine playoff berths seemed attainable — before turning sour.

Saturday's match was a microcosm of the season: a thin roster, a decent effort, not enough quality in the attack and ultimately a 1-0 loss to complete a 7-15-12 season. NYC's 87th-minute counterattack resulted in a three-on-one break from the midfield circle and Talles Magno's goal.

Fans began heading for the exits, too chilly or perhaps too bruised by the rash of bad seasons to express their discontent with an organization that has left them in the cold for years now.

Behind the north goal, where the supporters' groups gather, a banner lay across several seats: "We Deserve Better."

images.caption: Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. (Scott Taetsch via Getty Images)

articles.title: Ryan Day Reacts to OSU's Back-to-Back Losses vs. Oregon, USC, 'Didn't Expect Any of This to Happen'
articles.summary: Ohio State football entered this season as the No. 1 team in the polls, but the Buckeyes' College Football Playoff hopes are squarely on the brink after back-to-back losses to USC (30-18) and Oregon (41-28).
articles.body:
Ohio State football entered this season as the No. 1 team in the polls, but the Buckeyes' College Football Playoff hopes are squarely on the brink after back-to-back losses to USC (30-18) and Oregon (41-28).

It's natural for Buckeye Nation to feel stunned after OSU's midseason downfall, and needless to say, head coach Ryan Day feels the same way per his postgame comments after Saturday's Oregon loss.

Ohio State has been without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, who suffered an undisclosed right arm injury after a sack in the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes' 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17.

Still, OSU has taken a precipitous nosedive, and the season reached its ultimate low point Saturday as Oregon scored 38 unanswered points over 29 minutes and 24 seconds of game time.
