articles.title: LSU's Reality-Check Loss to Alabama Turns the Pressure Up on Lane Kiffin
articles.summary: At LSU, you're either winning national championships or you're in the process of being fired. There is no compromise. No grace periods. No moral victories. You either win huge, or you lose huge, no matter the circumstances.
articles.body:
At LSU, you're either winning national championships or you're in the process of being fired. There is no compromise. No grace periods. No moral victories. You either win huge, or you lose huge, no matter the circumstances.

Lane Kiffin knows this. In fact, he left an incredible situation at Ole Miss to fully embrace the potential and pressure that LSU has to offer. He not only accepted this reality, he sprinted away from a College Football Playoff team and a potential national championship contender to take on this responsibility head on.

On Saturday night, however, he got his first taste of what this job is really like.

With the sport in a state of disarray, many were wondering if LSU was perhaps the best team in the country after all. The defense has been excellent, and the offense has shown flashes while getting pieces healthier.

In many respects, it made sense. LSU checks a lot of boxes.

After an ugly, sloppy 31-13 loss to Alabama at home, that momentum is all but gone. Instead, Kiffin faces a new reality as he heads into the season's home stretch.

LSU did plenty of good things on Saturday afternoon, tallying 485 yards of offense to Alabama's 285. That's part of the story and the anguish that will carry into the week ahead.

The Tigers, however, could never find the breakthrough moment, turning the ball over twice and failing on four fourth-down attempts.

The Tigers had plenty of chances, and they couldn't quite capitalize. In the moments they came up short, the camera often fixated on Kiffin as he nervously paced the sideline.

The strain was evident. Some coaches, like Kalen DeBoer on the other sideline, coach with a poker face, rarely showing any emotion at all.

Not Kiffin, and certainly not Kiffin on this day. Knowing just how important this game was for his season and his reputation, he didn't hold anything back.

For LSU, this is a crushing blow. The Tigers are now 6-3 with two games against ranked teams still to come. They came into the week ranked No. 14 by the College Football Playoff selection committee, and they will drop. We'll find out how far on Tuesday.

Historically, a third loss was a deathblow for playoff hopes. Although in 2026, with the committee showing plenty of love for the SEC early on, that might not be the case.

Still, what happened on Saturday is crushing, especially when you consider that LSU plays Texas and Tennessee on the road in consecutive weeks.

The good news? There are still two enormous opportunities to make an impression.

The bad news? One more loss and any hopes of making it to the postseason are all but dead, and even now things don't look great.

At LSU, that is unacceptable. Forget about how quickly the roster came together and all the good Kiffin has done in his first season, and he's done plenty to offer hope for the future.

The losses are always much bigger than the wins. And the failures linger for much longer than the successes that seem to wash away a few days later. This one will sting for some time.

None of this, of course, is a surprise to Kiffin.

He's coached for Nick Saban. He knows precisely how much 60 minutes of football mean each and every week. And he's spent enough time in the SEC to realize what a loss of this magnitude, especially at home to a rival, can do to momentum for a season or a program.

All that said, Kiffin isn't on the hot seat. Let's be clear about that for anyone questioning otherwise. It would be foolish to suggest as such.

LSU has invested too much money in the coach to make such a declaration. Given what it took to get him in Baton Rouge, LSU will give its new head coach plenty of opportunities to deliver.

But on Saturday, Kiffin didn't get any closer to winning a national championship. In fact, until further notice, the prospects seem unlikely.

With that acknowledged, and with the expectations at LSU unchanged, the outcome only points in one direction.

If Kiffin was looking for a true taste of what coaching at LSU is like, he just got it.
